as_told.title: Priest of Sais tells Solon about cyclic cataclysm

plain: Solon, a lawmaker of ancient Athens, is said to have heard the story of Atlantis, a great lost island civilisation, from Egyptian priests at a temple of the goddess Neith in Sais, a city in the Nile Delta. The writer Graham Hancock, who argues for lost ancient civilisations, tells it twice from the account left by the Greek philosopher Plato in his dialogues Timaeus and Critias. Hancock says the priests read hieroglyphs, the old Egyptian picture-writing, off the temple wall to Solon and translated them for him. That, he says, is why Plato gives such an early date: Solon's visit around 600 BC, and Atlantis around 9600 BC. The filmmaker Tim Alberino also brings up the priest of Sais teaching Solon, but he stresses a different lesson: that the world goes through repeated cycles of great disasters, which he ties to our own age. Both men are summarising the ancient texts, not new evidence. The story matters to them because it would mean a real memory of a lost civilisation was kept in Egypt.
